name: TerraFirma
what: Tech-enabled, vertically integrated construction company: retrofits excavators, dozers, loaders, rollers and skid steers for remote/semi-autonomous operation, runs them from its own command-and-control center with in-house pre-construction software, and performs the earthwork itself on commercial and government contracts.

Owner-operated AI-native steel fabrication plant in Cincinnati run on in-house Factory OS; sells complex welded structural steel assemblies (frames, skids, enclosures, modular infrastructure) to energy, utility, industrial and modular-construction buyers.

name: Machina Labs
what: Software-defined factories that form, weld, assemble and finish complex metal structures with AI-guided robots, no dedicated tooling; aerospace and defense customers.

name: Re:Build Manufacturing
what: PE-style roll-up of US manufacturers with a shared tech layer. Comp for 'buy plants + add software' vs greenfield.

name: SendCutSend
what: Instant-quote online sheet-metal and CNC service that owns and runs its own factories (laser, waterjet, bending, machining, finishing); bootstrapped-style growth to a $1B valuation.

name: Senra Systems
what: Designs and manufactures aerospace wire harnesses in its own plant on proprietary software (digital-twin conversion, automated work instructions, live status) plus automation.

name: Arda
what: AI agent for manufacturing engineers: reads CAD and design docs and produces assembly order, work instructions and station layouts for lines in plants owned by others; robot-programming agents and a factory-video model are roadmap. Co-founded by ex-OpenAI chief research officer Bob McGrew.

name: Mind Robotics
hq: Palo Alto, CA (site); Sunnyvale per Harmonic
what: Rivian spinout building full-stack factory robots (models, hardware, deployment infra) trained on video of skilled operators on live automotive lines; Rivian's Normal, IL plant is the first customer and training site; no humanoids.

name: Rockwell Automation
what: Industrial automation hardware and software

name: CuspAI
hq: Cambridge, UK (offices Amsterdam, Berlin, Tokyo, US; Singapore opening)
what: Generative AI plus molecular simulation for materials discovery, sold through the 'AI Materials Foundry': a consortium of 45+ industry, lab and data partners where CuspAI's MIRA platform designs candidates and partner labs synthesize and test them. Use cases: semiconductor materials, coatings, membranes/sorbents, catalysts, batteries.

name: Periodic Labs
what: AI research and deployment company: builds 'AI scientists' and the autonomous robotic labs they run in; robots synthesize powders and test them, results (including failures) train the next round. Monetizes today by deploying custom AI agents into industrial R&D (semiconductor heat dissipation); long-term target is higher-temperature superconductors.

name: Radical AI
hq: New York, NY (lab in midtown Manhattan; moving to Brooklyn Navy Yard)
what: Owns and runs a self-driving materials lab in NYC: AI proposes alloy compositions, a robotic line mixes, melts, characterizes and tests them (up to 50 experiments/day, targeting 100), and results feed back into the model. First products are high-temperature alloys for jet engines, defense and fusion; a Purdue torch test showed 125x survivability vs C103.

name: ATI
what: Titanium and nickel specialty materials and forgings

name: Carpenter Technology
what: Specialty alloys (nickel, cobalt, titanium) for aerospace

name: Mariana Minerals
hq: San Francisco, CA (ops: Houston; Copper One in San Juan County, UT; Lithium One in East Texas)
what: Software-first, vertically integrated critical-minerals producer that acquires brownfield assets and builds and operates its own mines and refineries (copper, lithium; then uranium, rare earths, nickel, cobalt, manganese, magnesium) on in-house MarianaOS (MineOS, PlantOS, CapitalProjectOS).

name: Nox Metals
hq: Detroit, MI (Southwest Detroit); roles also in Los Angeles and San Francisco
what: YC S25 owner-operated automated metals service center: buys aluminum plate/block from foundries and cuts to size on an automated line, with in-house quoting and order-to-job software (quotes in minutes vs 3-5 days from brokers). Steel, tube and sheet on the roadmap.

name: Nucor
what: Largest US steelmaker; electric-arc minimills; benchmark for metals margins and reshoring narrative.

name: Reliance (Reliance Steel & Aluminum)
what: Largest North American metals service center. Benchmark for service-center economics and M&A.

name: Ryerson
what: Public metals service center (cut-to-size, processing). The incumbent Nox Metals is rebuilding.

name: Divergent Technologies
what: Divergent Adaptive Production System (DAPS): in-house generative design, metal additive manufacturing and automated fixtureless robotic assembly in its own Torrance plant; sells parts and structures as a certified Tier 1 supplier to automotive, aerospace and defense, and pitches DAPS as 'design-manufacturing-assembly as a service'.

name: Freeform
what: Builds its own multi-laser metal AM machines (GoldenEye, 18 lasers; Skyfall, hundreds of lasers) with in-house sensors, FPGA/GPU controls and ML that monitor and correct the melt in real time, and runs them as a parts service for aerospace, defense, space and energy customers; does not sell printers.

name: Hadrian
hq: Torrance, CA (HQ); factories in Torrance CA, Mesa AZ, Cherokee AL
what: Autonomous precision-parts factories for aerospace, defense and now naval shipbuilding: CNC machining, inspection and scheduling run by its in-house Opus software stack; sells parts to primes and 'factories-as-a-service' capacity to DoD programs.

name: Howmet Aerospace
what: Castings, forgings, fasteners for aero engines and IGT

name: Isembard
hq: London, UK (first factory Harlesden, NW London)
what: Network of software-defined precision machining facilities in the UK/Europe for aerospace, defense and energy; rebuilding sovereign precision-parts capacity.

name: Precision Castparts (Berkshire)
what: Incumbent in aerospace castings/forgings; the capacity startups are selling against.

name: Proto Labs
what: Public digital manufacturer that owns its plants (injection molding, CNC, sheet metal, 3D printing). Closest public owner-operator comp for GM/capex.

name: Xometry
what: Public marketplace for custom parts; no plants (asset-light). The anti-thesis comp: software without owning production.
